body: Mali has very limited Street View coverage with only ten small trekker sets across seven locations; easier to memorise their appearance than geography.
Coverage uses a consumer-grade camera on a tripod, giving images motion blur, saturated colours, and an 'ethereal' look distinct from backpack trekker shots.
Tripods mostly document historic mosques made from mud bricks and adobe plaster, decorated with wooden sticks and prayer rugs inside.
Mosque exteriors can resemble normal streets and sometimes provide enough detail for competitive pinpointing, unlike their interiors.
Mali's arid landscapes with sandy, dry terrain help distinguish its tripods from those in other countries.
Niono mosque sits by a wide sandy road in a busy area, with nearby trees; locate via the Centre Commercial north of Niono’s centre.
Niono mosque interior features distinctive European-style pillars unique among Mali's covered mosques.
Sidi Yahiya mosque area has sand mixed with 'bread-slice' tiles, peach-orange brick buildings, and a busier vibe than Djingareyber.
Sidi Yahiya interior has yellow upper walls, unpainted brick below, and a courtyard with bright square tiles.
Djingareyber mosque exterior features brick buildings and paved streets with rectangular tiles.
Djingareyber mosque interior has yellow walls, wide rounded archways, and red carpeting.
Sankoré Mosque sits on sandy ground and has a distinctive pyramid-shaped tower.
Sankoré Mosque doors are richly decorated wood with metal details.
Sankoré interior has blue carpet, yellow walls, and low ceilings supported by wooden beams.
Gao mosque exterior shows a large empty space with reddish dirt and scattered trees.
Gao mosque interior has plain corridors with low roofs and a courtyard view of a branch-covered pyramid structure.
Djenné mosque front is iconic, in an open area with low houses and distant trees under a clear sky.
Djenné interior is dark, with a high roof, gothic arches, and a sandy courtyard with wooden doors.
Mopti mosque resembles Djenné but has closer trees, slight clouds, and narrower surrounding streets.
Mopti interior is open, with a high roof, no arches, and full blue carpeting.
Empty modern mosque in NW Bamako has light blue walls, pink floor, and misplaced coverage actually in rural Mali.
Bandiagara Escarpment gorge has dry trees and bushes along the rocky path southwest of Sangha Ogol Leye.
Within Sankoré mosque coverage are misplaced images of a Bamako tour business, classroom, streets, and other unrelated locations.
